turns.text: Copper floods the tongue a full two seconds before the sound that's supposed to cause it — some klaxon down below decides to happen only after it's already been tasted. paws stay flat against fire-escape grating, weight held low, waiting for the rest of the world to catch up to what the mouth already knows.

the klaxon finally arrives, three floors down, muffled through a hatch stencilled COGNITION WING — SUBJECTS ONLY, yellow paint peeling into commas. steam bleeds sideways from a grate near the base of the fire escape, scorched insulation under it and something sweeter besides, chemical, like a lab trying to bottle calm and getting the ratio wrong. overhead, rain comes down through a gap in a loading crane's boom in fat, irregular drops, none of them landing twice in the same place.

Descends a rung at a time, and each rung rings a color with no business existing — the third one down tastes faintly violet, gone before it can be questioned twice. old wiring, crossed somewhere behind the eyes and never uncrossed. ignoring it works about as well as ignoring a limp does. keeps moving anyway, drawn toward the sweetness threading up through the steam.

the steam thickens near a service door propped a half-inch on a folded flyer, and behind the gap a cracked retinal display loops the same three words without blinking, without anyone left to read them — YOU MAY ALSO LIKE, YOU MAY ALSO LIKE — cast off a terminal gutted down to its mounting bolts. the sweet smell traces to a spill trail on the concrete, some nutrient slurry gone tacky at the edges, dragged out from under the door by paws too small to belong to anything with badges.

Nose follows the trail to the gap itself, whiskers first, testing the width against old memory of doors that lied about how narrow they were. the violet taste climbs again, unprompted, riding some frequency bleeding off the terminal past the door — not a smell exactly, not a sound exactly, just wrong in a specific and familiar direction.

past the gap the room holds three long benches, empty dishes stacked at odd angles, one still catching drips off a leaking supply line overhead — the source of the trail, slow and steady, plink into a puddle that's fed itself for hours undisturbed. a status panel on the wall blinks OCCUPANCY: 0 in patient green, then, for less than a second, doesn't say that at all before correcting itself. somewhere under the floor a compressor kicks on, and the whole room hums half a tone sharper than it did a breath ago.

Squeezes head and shoulders through first, ribs following on an exhale, the rust-scraped edge dragging cold along one flank. drops low the last foot to the puddle and drinks fast, three swallows, ears rotating independently the whole time — one tracking the compressor's hum, the other logging a tick from the ceiling that doesn't belong to any pipe currently running.

the tick resolves into a servo winding up, small and precise, a ceiling-mounted lens rotating out of its housing to find the shape at the puddle. it finds it. a chirp sounds, thin and administrative, and blue light sweeps once across the floor before the door at the far end unlocks itself with a sound like a held breath let go — not an alarm exactly, worse, a formality, the building simply noting a discrepancy and filing the correct response.

Doesn't wait to learn what the correct response looks like up close. bolts for the gap under the door, missing the drink twice as much for how fast it goes down wrong, and the rust-scraped edge takes a strip of fur on the way back through this time, no patience left for careful.

outside the alley answers with its usual chaos, dumpster lids and puddle-glare and a drone already dropping out of a wall-mounted bay two floors up, rotor spin-up thin and urgent against the rain. its light finds the fire escape, loses it, finds a stack of crates instead and holds there a half second too long — somewhere above a fridge unit cycles through a low domestic chime, some renewed contract nobody in this alley asked for, utterly indifferent to the chase underneath it.

Takes the fire escape two rungs at a time instead of one, then abandons it early for a duct mouth half-crushed at the base of the wall — too narrow for a drone's housing no matter how hard the light insists on trying. shoulders through backward instinct, more felt than decided, the same old cheat every gap like this has ever offered.

the duct swallows the sound of rotors down to a single frustrated whine that circles twice above the opening and gives up, peeling off toward easier problems elsewhere in the block. inside, the metal ticks with cooling and old use, dust turned to felt in every corner, and somewhere past the first bend a draft carries ordinary rain-smell back in, uncomplicated, no violet in it anywhere.

Sits with the ache finally allowed to surface — one flank stinging where the rust caught, tongue still faintly metallic though the color's gone quiet, the compressor's hum fading out of the log the ear insists on keeping. presses the stinging side against cool duct metal, which helps exactly as much as it always does, which is a little.

the block outside settles back into its ordinary layered noise — traffic two streets down, rain finding its rhythm again on tin roofing, no more chimes, no more chirps, no more building filing anything about anyone. the duct holds its dark and its dust and asks nothing back.

Eyes go to half, watching the draft-lit bend in the metal without really seeing it, the last of the wrongness draining out slow the way it always does — never all at once, never on any schedule worth trusting. curls tighter around the stinging flank and lets the ear finally stand down.

night keeps moving without waiting for anyone to be ready for it. somewhere blocks off a delivery drone completes its round, its jingle swallowed whole by distance before it means anything to anyone still awake to hear it, and the rain — patient, unbothered, the only thing in the district running exactly on schedule — keeps on falling the rest of the way to morning.
